page0.text:
"...So hot."
I open my eyes. I can't sleep.
My pajamas are heavy with sweat. I kick off the covers.
I wipe my forehead, finding that it's slick with enough sweat to soak a kitchen rag.

page1.text:
...
...I can't think straight.
Did the summer-like heat cook my brain?
I think as hard as I can, but I can't tell what, when, or where this is.
...
I go out into the yard.
I just want to cool off my burning body.
...Was the room hot, or was it just me?
Thinking is a pain, so I'll sleep in the shed tonight.
It's cold in there.
It doesn't matter whether it's hot or—

page2.text:
"Guh... Argh...!"
Suddenly, stabbing pain drives me to my knees.
"...Argh..."
I keel over, panting hard.

page3.text:
...I'm awake.
I clutch my left arm, the source of the heat and pain.
It's wrapped in a holy shroud.
The red cloth locks the arm up tight.
I can move it, but it's wrapped so tightly the blood is cut off.
Then, I wonder if it's the cloth that's hurting my arm.

page4.text:
"Maybe it'll actually go back to normal if I take this off."
It's a terribly enticing delusion.
I haven't even seen what's under the red cloth yet.
It's not that I don't believe what the priest said, but what if he's wrong?
